grounding.derivation: The developer documentation describes commitment as durable quorum replication, and FSM.Apply's interface comment makes commitment a prerequisite. The implementation produces persistence reports and aggregates them before application scheduling. This establishes audit significance without proving that any particular report or configuration is valid.

grounding.derivation: commitment.match documents that a report means a server's disk agrees through an index. replicateTo invokes updateLastAppended after success. appendEntries can delete a conflicting suffix and then return after StoreLogs fails without reaching setLastLog; its comment explicitly notes stale last-log state. The next request may consult a cached last entry. Whether this can produce false support depends on accessors, legal request construction and the response-to-report mapping.
grounding.applicability: Candidate producer/consumer obligation for acknowledgments actually used as match evidence. A failed request itself returns Success=false and therefore does not demonstrate a violation.
unresolved: Whether stale metadata survives to a relevant successful request
Whether storage failure requires process termination outside this handler
Whether later guards or recovery prevent consumption
alternatives: Request construction or updateLastAppended may prevent credit from an empty successful request.
A retry containing replacement entries may repair history before credit is produced.
An applicable adapter or hosting contract may terminate the node after the relevant storage error.

bindings.excerpt:
func (r *Raft) setupLeaderState() {
	r.leaderState.commitCh = make(chan struct{}, 1)
	r.leaderState.commitment = newCommitment(r.leaderState.commitCh,
		r.configurations.latest,
		r.getLastIndex()+1 /* first index that may be committed in this term */)
	r.leaderState.inflight = list.New()
	r.leaderState.replState = make(map[ServerID]*followerReplication)
	r.leaderState.notify = make(map[*verifyFuture]struct{})
	r.leaderState.stepDown = make(chan struct{}, 1)
}

associations.rationale: Provides concrete sender-state construction, peer identity maintenance and stop signaling needed to constrain admissible request histories.

bindings.description: Constructs replication state for configured nonlocal peers with the current commitment pointer, current term and nextIndex=getLastIndex()+1; starts and triggers replication. Existing instances retain their state when the peer address changes. Removed instances receive a final index, have stopCh closed and are removed from the map.

bindings.description: Sets up leader state, registers deferred cleanup, starts peer replication, dispatches a no-op and enters leaderLoop. Deferred cleanup closes replication stop channels and clears leader-owned references; no join of replication workers is visible in this range.
pending: Closing stop channels does not by itself establish that outstanding work cannot complete or report afterward.
Worker termination, outstanding transport futures and isolation from subsequent leader lifetimes require their actual implementations.
Calls to dispatchLogs and leaderLoop do not independently establish those callees' behavior.
